## Access — behind the gateway door

Who may enter: {{accessWho}}. Sign-in is Firebase Authentication in `{{authProject}}`; a person's groups are the
custom claim `groups`, granted only with the monorepo's `node scripts/grant-groups.mjs` (docs/runbooks/platform-auth.md).
{{#if accessNote}}
Access note: {{accessNote}}
{{/if}}

{{#if doorActive}}
- Hosting rewrites `{{path}}{,/**}` to Cloud Run `{{gatewayService}}` (the gateway door), not to `{{service}}`. The door opens the
  browser's sealed `__session`, re-checks its groups against the current registry, then forwards the full path to {{directUrl}}.
{{/if}}
{{#unless doorActive}}
- The door is off ({{doorOffReason}}): Hosting routes `{{path}}` straight to Cloud Run `{{service}}`, so the platform URL is
  unguarded until the door is switched back on.
{{/unless}}
- Entering: `POST {{path}}/__door/session` with `Authorization: Bearer <Firebase ID token>` → 200 and a sealed `__session`
  cookie (`Path={{path}}`, HttpOnly, at most {{sessionHours}} h) · 401 `sign_in_required` · 403 `group_required`.
  `DELETE {{path}}/__door/session` leaves. The portal does this for you when you walk through the gate.
- Refusals: a page load (GET with `Accept: text/html`) is redirected 303 to
  `/?gate={{id}}&reason=<sign_in_required|group_required|session_expired|door_unconfigured>`; any other request gets JSON 401/403/503.
{{#if hasApi}}
- Gateway API: `{{gatewayUrl}}…` needs `Authorization: Bearer <ID token>` that passes the same policy; only
  `{{gatewayAppHealthUrl}}` stays public.
{{/if}}
- The app still sets its own `__session` (contract rule 3): the door keeps it inside the sealed envelope and hands it back
  on every request, so keep its value under about 2 KB.
{{/if}}

{{/if}}

```bash
{{#if routingReady}}

{{/unless}}
{{#if doorActive}}

curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' {{platformUrl}}   # the same without accept: text/html → 401 JSON
{{#if hasApi}}
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' {{gatewayAppHealthUrl}}   # the guarded app's one public API route → 200
{{/if}}
{{/if}}
{{/if}}
{{#unless routingReady}}
# {{platformUrl}} is expected to fail until routing.ready is true; test the direct host only
{{/unless}}
```

## How to interact

- {{authNote}}
{{#if hasAccess}}
- Through the platform, sign in to {{domain}} first and walk through the {{name}} gate; the portal opens the door for the browser. Without a
  platform session, use the direct host (with `Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-identity-token)` once `allUsers` is gone).
{{/if}}
- Every path the app serves lives under `{{path}}` on both hosts (Hosting passes the full path through). Locally, run with the base path set and open `http://localhost:<port>{{path}}/`.
- Platform contract v1 (site-plugin skill) applies: relative redirects, all browser state in one `__session` cookie with `Path={{path}}`, a health route answering `{"status","app","version","commit","deployedAt"}`, and deploys that set `APP_VERSION`, `APP_COMMIT` and `APP_DEPLOYED_AT` with `--update-env-vars`.
- Source of truth: the `{{id}}` entry in `registry/registry.json` (URLs, status, api, access, repo); CI patches its `deployment` block from the version and commit the health route reports (every 30 minutes) or from a `register-app` call. Edit the registry, then rerun `node plugins/eisen-platform/skills/site-plugin/scripts/generate-site-skills.mjs`.
